full_judgment:
2. The facts as stated in the petition briefly, are that the petitioner is the proprietor of Messrs Jamil Trading Company. The respondent No. 2 being plaintiff filed Mortgage Suit No. 26 of 2001 on May, 2001 against the petitioner and his two guarantors for realisation of Taka 42,96,879 as on 30th April, 2001. The petitioner in course of his business at one time fell short of cash flow and applied to the respondent bank by a letter dated 23-2-95 to sanction revolving LTR (Loan Against Trust Receipt) for an amount of Taka 50 lac in a bid to release some goods covered by the letter of credit opened by the petitioner in the respondent bank. The respondent bank failed to sanction the said sum although the L/C was secured by the documents of title of the imported goods and there was also full security for the proposed revolving LTR. As a result the petitioners imported goods were auctioned by the authorities which made the petitioner to incur a huge loss for failure and negligence by the respondent bank. The L/C good were hypothecated in favour of the bank. The respondent bank failed to provide the revolving LTR and therefore was unable to obtain possession of the L/C goods and in the process failed to stop the auction process and avoid the loss to the petitioner. After long four months of the petitioner's application on 25th June, 1995 for revolving LTR, the respondent bank sanctioned the revolving LTR for a sum of Taka 40 lac against further security to cover the forced loan created in respect of the goods auctioned earlier. The petitioner had already repaid the respondent bank the sums due under the letter of credit opened earlier. Although the forced loan was ultimately of no use to the petitioner as he had already incurred loss due to late sanction by the respondent bank, nevertheless the petitioner had already paid almost 75% of the principal amount of the loan. Despite regular repayments made by the petitioner the respondent bank filed Mortgage Suit No. 26 of 200 1 against the petitioner-the Firm Messrs Jamil Trading Company and the two guarantors. In the suit the respondent bank did not serve summons upon the petitioner personally and the petitioner had no way to know that a suit was filed against him. On 29th July, 2001 the respondent No. 1 the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Chittagong by Order No.5 ordered publication of notice to the petitioner in two newspapers as per section 5(Ka) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. Pursuant to the said order notices were published on 2nd August, 2001 in two Bangla newspapers, namely, the Daily Azker Chattagram and the Daily Azker Kagoj. The said order and publications were contrary to the requirements of section 5(Ka) and that no publication was made in an English newspaper as provided under the said section. The petitioner has come to know of the suit and the preliminary decree very recently and the petitioner felt aggrieved that he was not given an opportunity to contest the suit. The summons that was published was defective and therefore the decree passed was an irregular decree and illegal one. It is contended that the impugned preliminary decree is an irregular decree liable to be set aside and sections 6 and 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 are contrary to the petitioner's fundamental right to justice as guaranteed under the Constitution. Even if sections 6 and 7 are found to be valid that should not apply in case of an irregular decree which was passed in breach of procedural rules set down in the Ain or in the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 3. The respondent No. 2 has filed an affidavit-in-opposition. Denying the material allegations the respondent bank has stated that despite repeated written and verbal reminders the petitioner did not come forward to adjust its liabilities in LTR facility to the respondent Bank. The respondent bank served a legal notice upon the petitioner through its lawyer on 13-2-2000 and requested the petitioner to adjust his outstanding dues with up to date interest. After receiving the notice although the petitioner promised to pay his outstanding dues by his letter dated 13-6-2000 but ultimately, did not take any step to adjust the liability and then the respondent bank filed the Mortgage Suit No. 26 of 2001. The summons in the mortgage suit was issued several times at the address of the petitioner. Finally, the summons were published in the daily newspaper as per provisions of the Ain, 1990 and it is not true that he was totally unaware of the suit filed against him and his firm. As soon as the summons were published in the newspapers as per order of the Adalat under section 5(Ka) of the Ain it would be deemed that the notices have been duly served. Since the petitioner did not appear in the suit despite publication of summons in the national dailies the suit was decreed ex parte against the petitioner and the other defendants. Upon publication of the summons in the newspaper the defendant No.4 Mst. Golbahar Begum wife of Haji Saru Miah Sowdagar appeared in the suit on 27-9-01 and prayed for time for filing written statement. Defendant No.3 (Ka) to 3 (Ta) also appeared in the suit on 1-4-2002. It has been contended that sections 6(2) and 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 provided remedy against an ex parte decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat on depositing 50% of the decretal amount. Instead of complying with the provision of law the petitioner has filed the writ petition which is not maintainable. In the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition it has been stated that before publication of the summons under section 5(Ka) of the Ain the summons was issued on 12-6-01 by usual process and by registered post with AD which is evident from the order-sheet. 

 4. Mr Azmalul Hossain, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, has contended, pointing out the provision of section 5(Ka) of the Ain that the summons had not been duly served upon the defendant petitioner and the summons under order of the Adalat had not been published in accordance with the provision of section 5(Ka) of the A in as no summons was published in the English daily newspaper and therefore, the petitioner had no knowledge about the proceeding of the suit and the ex parte decree obtained by the respondent bank and consequently, the ex parte judgment and decree is an irregular judgment which has to be set aside on the ground of non-service of summons upon the petitioner. He has further contended that the provision for preferring appeal as laid down under section 7 and also the provision for setting aside the ex parte decree under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on depositing 50% of the decretal dues is not equally efficacious remedy as in that case the petitioner has to deposit a substantial amount to apply to set aside a decree which is irregular. It is his contention that the provision for deposition 50% of the decretal amount for setting aside the irregular decree is a denial to have access to justice and such provision is contrary to the provision of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution. He has further contended that sections 6 and 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 even if found valid law insofar as the provision for setting aside the ex parte decree under Order IX, rule 13 CPC or for an appeal against an ex parte decree upon depositing 50% of the decretal amount does not apply on its true construction of irregular judgment and decree as the judgment and decree has been passed on breach of the Rules of Procedure as provided in the Ain as well as in the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his submission and on the proposition that the decree is an irregular decree in breach of the Rules of Procedure he has cited some decisions of our jurisdiction as well as of English jurisdiction. Reference may firstly be made to the case of Md Abdur Rashid and another vs Abdul Barik and another, reported in 1984 BLD (AD) 83 where it has been observed that the provision of Order IX, rule 13 CPC clearly lays down that once it has been found that summons were not duly served, that by itself is sufficient for setting aside the ex parte decree. In paragraph 10 it has been stated- 

 Relying on the aforesaid principle the learned Counsel has contended that for ex debito justitiae this Court on the ground of non-service of summons upon the defendant in breach of the procedural rules can set aside the ex parte decree which is not valid in the eye of law and that is the fundamental and constitutional right of the defendant to challenge the decree on the ground of breach of the Rules of Procedure. He has referred to us portion of the order-sheet and pointed out that summons upon the present petitioner was not duly served and the summons was not published in the newspaper complying with the provision of section 5(Ka) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. He has concluded his submission by referring the provision of the Constitution that the petitioner has not been treated in accordance with law as provided under Article 31 of the Constitution and for imposing the condition that to set aside the ex parte decree requiring the petitioner to deposit 50% of the amount decreed, the petitioner has been denied the access to justice. 

 6. Mr Morshed Ahmed Khan, the learned Advocate, on the other hand, has contended that sections 6 and 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 had already been repealed and there is no legal necessity of declaring the two sections as invalid and unconstitutional. He has, placing the supplementary affidavit and also the relevant order of the Court, argued that the summons was issued by the Adalat both by registered post and in usual course by process server and as the petitioner did not appear, subsequently the summons was published in the newspaper in accordance with the provision of section 5(Ka) of the Ain and there has been due service of summons upon the defendant-petitioner. He has argued that the other defendants in the suit appeared before the Court and prayed for time for filing written statement but they did not appear at the time of hearing and consequently the ex parte decree was passed. His further contention is that there is a specific provision under section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain to prefer an appeal for setting aside the decree and also provision for setting aside the ex parte decree under Order IX, rule 13 CPC after fulfilling the requirement of that Ain ie by depositing 50% of the decretal amount. Having not availed of that opportunity as the alternative remedy the writ petitioner has come up before this Court to have the decree set aside on the ground of non-service of summons and, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable. Mr Khan has placed his reliance in the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank Ltd. and others, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191 where the contention had been raised to the effect that to make a deposit of half of the decretal dues is no efficacious remedy for the petitioner and that submission was made relying on the case of Nagina Silk Mill, Lyallpur vs Income Tax Officer, Lyallpur, 15 DLR (SC) 181 and the Appellate Division held that the submission is misconceived and stated that
